correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly lists and exhausts the complete labeled orbit for m,n>=2, derives a symmetric N-regular operator, reduces it into 6+2(m-1)+2(n-1)+(m-1)(n-1) dimensions, exactly factors its characteristic polynomial, and proves all quartic Laplacian roots >1 by polynomial coefficient positivity. Exact independent graph-neighborhood BFS and symbolic char-polynomial verification pass for 16 size pairs; finite tests support but do not substitute for the general proof.

originality.rationale: Qualitative biclique LC orbit structure is known from Tzitrin and explicitly not claimed as new. Adcock et al. catalog limited-size orbit graphs and explicitly suggest mathematically investigating mixing rates, but do not present this full labeled biclique Markov spectrum and universal sharp gap. Closest retrieved published spectral walks use inequivalent state spaces. No stronger covering spectral theorem was identified in inspected literature; residual risk of unindexed equivalence is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper using a different name for the same weighted graph-state-orbit Markov operator could contain an equivalent spectrum.
The spectral result is for a classical Markov process on LC-equivalent graph-state representatives and should not be confused with coherent quantum-walk mixing.

value.rationale: Adcock et al. identify the random-LC mixing-rate question in quantum-network scrambling. The full analytic spectral decomposition for arbitrary biclique part sizes and the size-sharp relaxation time settle a motivated infinite-family case beyond the prior finite tables. Distinguishing one-sided from absolute gap prevents an unjustified total-variation claim.
